name: Congenital Vertical Talus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Vertical Talus

criteria.description: Rigid dorsal dislocation of the navicular on the talus
Fixed plantar-flexion of the talus bone
Rigid flatfoot with a convex plantar surface
Lateral radiographs showing vertical talus with talocalcaneal angle > 45 degrees

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of rigid dorsal dislocation of the navicular on the talus and radiographic confirmation of vertical talus deformity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic imaging; early diagnosis is critical for optimal treatment outcomes.

searchTerms: joint out of place in leg
excess bone growth at fracture site

imaging: Lateral foot radiograph showing vertical talus with dorsal dislocation of navicular
Increased talocalcaneal angle on lateral view (>45 degrees)
Absence of normal talonavicular joint congruity
genetic: Possible association with genetic syndromes such as trisomy 18, Freeman-Sheldon syndrome, and other neuromuscular disorders
other: Physical examination revealing rigid flatfoot with convex plantar surface and palpable talar head

distinguishingFeatures: Clubfoot presents with cavus foot and adductus deformity rather than convex plantar surface
Talus is plantar-flexed but navicular is not dorsally dislocated
Foot is typically supinated rather than pronated
Usually presents later in childhood or adolescence with pain and limited motion
No rigid dorsal dislocation of navicular
Radiographs show abnormal fusion between tarsal bones

redFlags: Rigid dorsal dislocation of navicular bone
Severe fixed plantar-flexed talus with inability to dorsiflex ankle
Delayed diagnosis leading to progressive deformity and impaired ambulation
references: Dobbs MB, Gurnett CA. Update on clubfoot: etiology and treatment. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2009 May;467(5):1146-53.
Orphanet: Congenital vertical talus. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
Kuo KN, et al. Congenital vertical talus: diagnosis and treatment. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2015;23(3):160-8.
